meta.company: The Woobles (learn-to-crochet brand, Shark Tank alumni)
meta.thesis: The Woobles does not need cuter kits - it needs people who say 'I'm not crafty' to discover the kit is engineered so they can't fail, and the Can't Fail Club turns a finished Wooble into a receipt, not a promise.
meta.variant_angle: guaranteed-success demo campaign + judge keep-kit prop

business_problem: The Woobles sells confidence disguised as a craft kit: 200 analyzed reviews are overwhelmingly five-star with 'easy' and 'beginner' as the vocabulary, yet the brand competes as a cute craft product while its real differentiator - a patented can't-fail construction method - is buried in product copy [R1][R3][S1][S2].

objectives.text: Drive 220 attributed orders (workshop QR + online code WOOBLE10) in 45 days at ~$35 AOV
Capture 900 email/SMS signups via Can't Fail workshops and stitch-along funnels
Reach 1.0M Texas impressions and shift 'crochet is hard/for grandmas' to 'a kit that can't fail' - +12 pts among surveyed shoppers

methods.recruitment: 200 public Judge.me reviews on woobles.com, keyword-coded (collected 2026-11-07)
Woobles catalog/kit pages, starter bundles, social vs craft-store positioning
Intercept survey at workshop sites, pre vs post

findings.finding: 'Easy', 'beginner', 'instructions' dominate reviews - buyers describe succeeding when they expected to fail; the product vocabulary IS the positioning
Overwhelmingly five-star with complaints concentrated in shipping/stock issues - product satisfaction is a solved problem
Reviewers self-identify as non-crafters ('never crocheted', 'not crafty') - the buyer is not the craft audience; the brand still markets to it
'Finished my first' and gift mentions appear organically - the finished Wooble is social proof nobody is amplifying

assumptions.text: $4,500 paid social at ~$7 CPM = ~640K impressions + ~360K organic stitch-along content
8 Can't Fail workshop shifts at ~$300 each (table, kit stock, signage)
WOOBLE10 code: 10% off first kit; netted in revenue
Tools/printing $550 (hooks, yarn stock, signage, finished-Wooble display)
Repeat kit purchase ~30% within 90 days (series collectibility)

slides.title: Campaign Overview
bullets: Problem: reviews say 'easy' and 'beginner' over and over - but the brand still markets to people who already think they're crafty [R1][R3].
Solution: Can't Fail Club - workshops where everyone finishes a stitch, stitch-along funnels, finished-Wooble UGC, giftable bundles.
45-day goal: 220 orders, 900 captures, +12 pts 'crochet is easy' [O1-O3].
slides.notes: We sell the finish line, not the craft.

slides.title: The Product
bullets: Learn-to-crochet kits: pre-started yarn, hook, eyes, video instructions - $25-45 kits, licensed + original characters [S1].
The differentiator is engineering: pre-started rounds mean you literally cannot start wrong - reviews confirm it [R1].
The finished product is a giftable plush you made yourself - emotional receipt.
Sold DTC online; Shark Tank alumni; viral cozy-craft moment [S3].
slides.notes: Hold up a finished Wooble vs the kit - 'this becomes this, guaranteed.'

slides.title: Company & Position
bullets: Learn-to-crochet brand built for absolute beginners - 200+ verified reviews, viral growth, licensed character lines [S1][S2][S3].
Craft-kit market is growing with screen-fatigued beginners, but competitors sell to crafters - Woobles sells to the intimidated [S5][R3].
Positioning gap: 'cute craft kit' is owned; 'the kit that can't fail' is unclaimed.
Campaign claims the guarantee.

slides.title: Campaign Objectives
bullets: O1 (primary): 220 attributed orders via WOOBLE10 + workshop QR at ~$35 AOV [O1].
O2: 900 email/SMS captures from workshops + stitch-along [O2].
O3: 1.0M impressions; +12 pts 'crochet is easy/anyone can' on pre/post survey (n=150 + holdout) [O3].
Baseline: current list; week-0 survey; Shopify code report.

slides.title: Target Market
bullets: P1: craft-curious beginners 16-34 - want a hobby, fear failing, cozy/TikTok-craft curious, screen-fatigued; Austin metro [S4].
P2: gifters + parents 25-50 - giftable, wholesome, screen-free; online [R4].
P1 is repositioning growth; P2 is reliable revenue.

slides.title: Research Methodology & Results
bullets: Content analysis of 200 public Judge.me reviews (collected 2026-11-07), keyword-coded [R1-R4].
Digital shelf audit of 8 sources: kit pages, bundles, social vs craft-store positioning [S1][S5].
Pending: intercept survey (n=150) at workshop sites + 3 interviews - field kit ready.
Reviews are uniformly positive - the corpus proves satisfaction, and shows the marketing gap.

slides.title: Insights -> Campaign Decisions
bullets: [R1] 'Easy/beginner/instructions' dominate -> sell the guarantee, not the plush: 'Can't Fail' is the theme.
[R2] Zero product complaints -> nothing to fix; the campaign is pure positioning + access.
[R3] Buyers call themselves non-crafters -> recruit the intimidated, not the crafty: workshops at campuses, not yarn shops.
[R4] 'Finished my first' + gift mentions -> make finishing the shareable moment: #cantfailclub UGC + gift bundles.

slides.title: Campaign Strategy
bullets: Theme: Can't Fail Club - membership you earn by finishing.
Push-pull: workshops create the first success (pull); stitch-along + gift drops convert at home (push) [R3][A4].
Finished Wooble as social proof: every finisher is an ad [R4].
PESO: paid geo-social, earned maker-fair/library PR, shared WIP/finish posts, owned email/SMS + stitch series.

slides.title: Budget & Financial Viability
bullets: Total $10,850: paid social $4.5K [A4]; creators $2.4K [A6]; workshops $2.4K [A7]; production $550 [A10]; contingency ~10% [A11].
Funnel: 1.0M impressions x 3% CTR x 0.7% purchase = ~210 orders = $7.4K revenue [A1][A4].
GP 50% = $3.7K; direct ROI ~-66% - an entry-proof budget: 900 captures + repositioning evidence; payback via 30% series repeat purchase [A2][A13].
Honest read: buying first-time crafters + community proof, not quarter margin [A15].

slides.title: Why It Matters
bullets: The Woobles already proved anyone can finish - it just hasn't told the people who need to hear it.
Can't Fail Club sells the finish line, not the craft - and hands the proof to the judge.
Every finisher is a customer and an ad: the product is its own case study.
